text:
Maya: quick sync — a handful of enterprise customers (EU & NA) asked for cross-region burst for Dedicated. want to capture tradeoffs on SLOs, isolation, and billing before we put this in the Q2 roadmap. any quick takes?

Sam: +1. Key decision: is geo-burst a routed fallback (best-effort, lower SLA) or a provisioned cross-region lane with committed capacity? different billing and isolation implications.

Diego: routed fallback is cheaper to implement (we already have routing + fallback today) but we cannot promise latency or strict availability. provisioned lane means reserved GPUs in each region -> predictable throughput & SLA, but more ops and cost.

Nina: customers are explicit: they want "burst across regions seamlessly when local capacity is saturated" and a billing model that doesn't feel like double-paying. they also want tenant isolation guarantees for regulated data.

Sam: propose three product patterns to evaluate: 
1) Best-effort geo-fallback: route to another region when local capacity not available. SLA: no hard SLA for bursts, only baseline region SLA remains. Billing: only charge when used. Implementation: short term.
2) Soft-reserved burst pockets: maintain small reserved pool in neighboring region that can be borrowed with soft-preempt. SLA: degraded SLA for burst (p99 latency guard, lower availability guarantee). Billing: subscription + usage.
3) Full multi-region reservation: customer reserves capacity in multiple regions; full SLA parity across regions. Billing: higher committed cost.

Diego: addition: eviction behavior needs to be explicit. options: soft-preempt (drain new requests off preemptible lanes), hard-evict (terminate lower-priority jobs). soft-preempt better UX but complex scheduler.

Maya: good list. we should also define launch criteria & metrics for each pattern. my draft: 
- Functional: cross-region routing, KV/kv-cache warmup strategy for redirected requests, consistent model variant selection (same model + quantization), observability per-route.
- SLOs: baseline region should keep existing SLA (e.g., p95 gen lat < 150ms). bursts: we call them "best-effort" or "degraded" — publish expected p95/p99 corridors and error uplift.
- Cost: published cost-per-token uplift for bursts + clear billing events.
- Security: data egress policy, KMS region constraints, and audit logs.

Sam: agree. also add quality guardrails: we need prompt/eval test harness to ensure model parity when falling back between regions. subtle tokenization/quantization differences can affect outputs.

Diego: infra notes: KV cache is the tricky part. warmup latency on a redirected request is high. we can mitigate with prefix caching and async prefetch for hot tenants. example config snippet for a soft-reserved lane: 
```yaml
lane: soft-reserved-eu->na
capacity: 200 concurrent tokens
preempt: soft
warmup: async-prefetch: true
sla: burst: best-effort
billing: committed: 0.2x monthly + usage uplift 1.3x
```

Nina: from PM ops: we need launch gating checklist: customer beta, 1 cross-region tenant in EU->NA, telemetry for: routing hits, failover rate, avg cold-warm latency delta, model mismatch rate, aborted requests. Without these we shouldn't declare GA.

rl-deploy-bot: deployment note — can create a canary cluster in us-west-2 to test routing + cache warmup. currently 3 free GPU nodes available.

Maya: decision proposal: iterate in this order: 
A) ship Best-effort geo-fallback as opt-in beta (low implementation cost). publish "best-effort" SLA language and cost uplift.
B) parallel prototype Soft-reserved pockets for top-tier customers (explicit reservation + soft-preempt). measure economics.
C) long-term: support Full multi-region reservation for large enterprise.

Sam: +1. timeline: A = 6wk spike + 4wk beta; B = 8-12wk design + customer pilot; C = Q4 planning.

Diego: action items: 
- Diego: build routing smoke test + add telemetry hooks (routing hits, fallback count, warmup delta) — ETA 2w.
- Sam: spec the fallback policy + canary config; add model parity checks; write production runbook — ETA 2w.
- Nina: identify pilot customers and draft billing proposal + launch gating checklist — ETA 1w.

Maya: I'll pull together a short PRD for the beta and schedule a 30m sync with infra + eng-platform next Tue. if anyone sees major missing items call out now.

Sam: one more: need clear customer-facing language: "burst is not covered by baseline SLA; we will endeavor to route and maintain model parity; billing is pay-for-what-you-use or reservation tiers" — legal needs to sign off.

Nina: noted. I'll loop legal on the billing copy.

Maya: perfect. saving action items in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-3942 (will attach PRD). thanks all :thumbsup:

Diego: +1. small follow-up: we should also run cost sims for 10, 30, 90 day patterns before B pilot.

Sam: adding that to spec.

rl-deploy-bot: created canary cluster ticket INF-3951 and assigned to Diego.

Maya: end — will update the roadmap doc after the sync.
